blocks.text: Why Finder feels slow for documentary filmmakers

Documentary work involves massive file counts. When you open a folder with 40,000 clips, Finder might struggle to draw the icons. This leads to the spinning beachball. Apple suggests keeping 10 to 15 percent of your startup disk free. This simple habit prevents the system from locking up during high-demand tasks.

items: Command + Up Arrow: Jump to the parent folder instantly.
Shift + Command + G: Open the Go to Folder box to paste a path.
Spacebar: Use Quick Look to preview video files without opening Premiere or Resolve.
Option + Command + P: Show the Path Bar so you know your exact location.
Shift + Command + N: Create a new folder for your dailies or project assets.

blocks.text: Never dump footage into a single folder. Create a structure that mirrors your project workflow. A common pattern is to have folders for Footage, Project Files, Audio, Graphics, and Exports. Use consistent naming. Start with the date in YYYY-MM-DD format. This keeps your files sorted chronologically by default.
Managing hidden files and system folders

Sometimes you need to access the Library folder or see hidden configuration files for your editing software. Press Shift + Command + Period to toggle hidden files in any Finder window. This is helpful when you need to clear cache files or locate preference files that are acting up.

Finder search often scans the entire drive. This is slow. Instead, ask Lazur to point at your target folder. You can ask Lazur to show you where a specific project directory is located. It draws a circle around the path. This keeps you focused on your work without digging through nested layers.

Finder is a core system process. It cannot be fully replaced. However, apps like ForkLift or Commander One offer dual-pane views. These help when you are moving large amounts of media from a camera card to a local RAID. Use these for heavy transfers. Keep using Finder for your daily project navigation.

faq.question: Can I replace Finder entirely?
faq.answer: No. Finder is a critical system process. You can use other apps for file management, but macOS requires Finder to handle the desktop and drive mounting.

faq.question: Why is my Finder slow with large folders?
faq.answer: Finder struggles with directories containing tens of thousands of items. Try grouping files by kind or using a list view to reduce the load on the system.

faq.question: How do I see file extensions?
faq.answer: Open Finder, go to Finder > Settings > Advanced, and check Show all filename extensions.
